title: Edgar Hayes band as his university: writing arrangements, copying Ray McKinley
summary: Joe Garland and Rudy Powell taught him writing; he made arrangements and copied the drumming on Ray McKinley's records.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, tell me something about it. What was that band like?
It was the most fantastic band.
Was it?
That was the school. That was the university for me.
Was it?
That was it.
Was it?
Oh, yeah.
Well, tell me.
Well, Joe Garland -- well, I had started writing then, with Joe Garland and Rudy Powell and all those guys in the band. They just taught me --
Oh, that's where it all began.
They taught me everything.
No kidding.
And I used to write for the band, you know, like, you remember when the "Goona-Goon," tunes like that?
Yeah.
I used to make arrangements on that.
Yeah.
And I used to copy Ray McKinley.
You did?
Yeah, I used to copy him.
No kidding.
He was with Tommy Dorsey at the time.
Well, he had his own band.
Yeah, he did.
You know. And that was before he joined Tommy. Was it Tommy's band? But he had his own band.
Yeah.
But I used to buy all his records. I used to buy all his records.
Well, that's interesting.
Isn't that something? And I'd copy Ray McKinley.
No kidding. Does he know that?
No, I don't think he knows. That's when I first --
That might make him feel real good.
